finding.claim: Stored SSRF: a user-supplied callbackUrl is saved at subscribe time and later requested server-side by notifyAll with no scheme, host or IP validation. An attacker can point it at internal services or cloud metadata (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and the server will POST the payload there on every run.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(), from the POST /subscribe body (Jobs.java:13)

trace.note: URL stored unvalidated in the subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates the stored callback URLs
client.send() issues the POST to the attacker-chosen URL

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, scheme check, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking or DNS-rebinding protection in subscribe() or notifyAll(). The only visible check is the try/throw in thumb(), which is a different path. The response body is discarded, so this is blind SSRF, but the POST still reaches internal endpoints. HttpClient does not follow redirects by default.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:13-14 store the attacker-supplied callbackUrl unvalidated, and src/Jobs.java:19-24 later POST to URI.create(cb) with no scheme/host/IP check (the regex guard at :30 only protects thumb()), so blind SSRF is reachable.
